title: Khloé Kardashian Recommends These 3 Episodes If You’re New to Her ‘Wonder Land’ Podcast
summary: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, Khloé Kardashian shares the episodes you should listen to if you’re new to her “Wonder Land” podcast ahead of its Season 4 premiere.
Khloé Kardashian says the first seasons of her “Khloé in Wonder Land” podcast were “trial and error” when it came to setting the tone for the project.
But as the podcast enters its fourth season, the 42-year-old reality star and entrepreneur is feeling confident and ready to continue quenching her curiosity on a number of topics.

“My mind goes anywhere and everywhere. I do want to learn from these experts and have things that are takeaways, and then I also want to talk to someone about spray tans and makeup,” Kardashian tells TODAY.com with a laugh. “And then I also want to go down some rabbit hole about aliens and the pyramids. I want to go everywhere.”

Her genuine curiosity is what has fueled the upcoming season of “Khloé in Wonder Land.” But first, she wants to kick off Season 4 with a “light and fun” episode with TV personality and “Summer House” alum Paige Desorbo.
“Wonder Land” contains multitudes, whether it’s a chat with a medical professional, her best friend or mom Kris Jenner. Kardashian hopes people “find a connection to one of the episodes.”
One conversation that is extra meaningful is her 2025 sit down with the late Dolly Parton.

“The one that I’ve held deepest in my heart is the one with Dolly Parton, which I feel privileged and blessed that I got to interview her,” she says. “And I believe I was like one of her last podcasts that she’s done. To be with her in Tennessee, what a blessing for me.”
Ahead of the “Khloé in Wonder Land” Season 4 premiere on Sept. 30, Kardashian shares the three episodes she recommends if you’re new to her podcast.
Making Contact with Extraterrestrials ft. Dr. Steven Greer

Kardashian’s sit down with Dr. Steven Greer, a leading expert on UFO disclosure, secret government operations and suppressed technology, aired on March 6, 2025. The two discussed theories on hidden alien technology, potential military cover-ups and more.
“If you’re into aliens and conspiracies, I loved my Dr. Steven Greer episode,” she says. “It was fascinating — and whatever you think, you think. But if you’re into it, great!”
Raising Resilient Kids, Setting Limits & Mom Guilt ft. Dr. Becky
Her June 5, 2025 episode with clinical psychologist Dr. Becky Kennedy was informative for Kardashian. The two unpacked mom guilt, setting boundaries, raising resilient children and more.

“I loved Dr. Becky when it came to kids and all the tips that I got from her for those,” the mom of two says, also adding, “How lucky am I that I sit on a couch, I’m asking them questions, but how many takeaways I get to implement into my life and pass on to other people.”
Kardashian adds that when it comes to guests who are experts, “the ones that actually are changing people and helping them, I feel really honored that I have a platform that can provide that.”
Untold Stories Behind the Kardashians ft. Kris Jenner
There’s one special guest that is always a good time, and that’s Kardashian’s mom, Kris Jenner.
Jenner has been on “Wonder Land” a number of times, delivering inside scoop, going down memory lane and sharing her wisdom with her daughter and listeners.

“I love the ones that I do with my mom. I love the nuggets that she gives you, whether it be motherly or silly or just, like, cutesy or some insight on our family,” Kardashian says. “But then she’ll also drop a few gems that you have to pick up along the way.”
Kardashian loves that Jenner has become everyone’s mother, saying, “Thank God, I love it, and she loves it too. It’s the best.”
New episodes of “Khloé in Wonder Land” will drop every Wednesday on YouTube and audio streaming services.

title: Would Jose Iglesias Ever Return to the MLB? What He Told Craig Melvin
summary: Although MLB player Jose Iglesias may have stepped away from baseball, he isn’t completely ruling out a return to the diamond.
story: Although MLB player Jose Iglesias may have stepped away from baseball, he isn’t completely ruling out a return to the diamond.

During his recent appearance on Craig Melvin’s “Glass Half Full” podcast, Iglesias was asked if he would ever consider playing baseball again if the opportunity arose. Iglesias last played in September 2025 for the Padres but has not formally retired from the league.
“If that phone rings, and it’s not Broadway and it’s MLB, I’ll be there because I feel good,” Iglesias told Craig.
Iglesias, 36, made his MLB debut in 2011 and became a free agent after the 2025 season. He’s most recently pivoted to Broadway, debuting in “Buena Vista Social Club” in August 2026.
While Iglesias said he would play in the MLB, he had one caveat.
“I have to have a personal feeling for the team,” he said. “I’m in that state of my life where (it’s) not just to play, but to play for something.”
He then named the two teams that already meet that: the New York Mets and the San Diego Padres.

Iglesias played for the New York Mets during the team’s 2024 Cinderella season, which culminated in a playoff run to the National League Championship. The Mets lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers, just missing a World Series appearance.

Iglesias was a fan favorite during the 2024 season after releasing the song “OMG” under his stage name Candelita. In addition to serving as his walk-up song, “OMG” became the team’s unofficial anthem that season.
The Mets did not resign Iglesias for the 2025 season, and he signed with the Padres.
Iglesias said both the Mets and Padres “opened the door” for him when he thought his career was ending, “so I have to show loyalty for both of them.”
“Any of those organizations would be a privilege, would be an honor,” he added. “And obviously, I hope it’s the Mets.”
“You just made a lot of people very happy,” Craig said.
He then offered Iglesias the hypothetical choice between another Broadway appearance and playing for the Mets.
“You know what? That will be an easy answer,”  Iglesias said. “New York Mets all day long.”

title: Hailey Bills May Be Eliminated on ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ But She’s Not Going Anywhere
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” pro Hailey Bills shares how life is like after being eliminated, what she hopes to do next and more.
story: “Take it From Me“ is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, Hailey Bills shares what life looks like for a pro after being eliminated on “Dancing With the Stars.”
Life for Hailey Bills is busy and she wouldn’t have it any other way.
The 20-year-old dancer made her debut as a pro on Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars,” partnered with Sarah Jane Nader to become the third same sex coupling on the show.
However, after a double elimination during premiere week, their time was cut short.

“I’m so sad to be eliminated, more so because Sarah Jane and I were honestly (becoming) best friends ... but we’re trying to stay in contact, hang all the time,” Bills tells TODAY.com. “But my schedule is just way different now. I’m still busy, but just in different ways.”
Life after elimination includes attending events and making appearances as a “DWTS” pro. She still has to rehearse (though not as much), and gets to be a part of the weekly show.

“We’re still considered pros. We’re just eliminated. I’m pretty sure it’s almost every week, I’ll still be doing some sort of performance,” Bills says. “I know they want to keep the eliminated pros doing performances, we’ll just keep adding a person every week.”
What that entails, she says, is creating new routines for the show.
“We’re choreographing some future numbers, some group numbers, and all the things like that,” she says. “You’ll still see us dancing.”

And fans did get a chance to see Bills perform alongside “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” winner and fellow new pro Adele Zaikman during Viral Hits Night. Both eliminated ladies entertained audiences during a transition during the Sept. 22 episode.
The Texas and Utah native has been dancing since she was a child, becoming a multiple-time national champion at The Dance Awards and a finalist in various national ballroom events.

She joined “DWTS” last season as part of the troupe, before becoming a pro this year. Her ties to the dancing competition show run deep, though. Bills’ aunt is current pro Jenna Johnson. She’s also toured with Derek Hough, who is a judge on “DWTS.”
While Bills’ first season competing on “DWTS” was short lived, she’s now looking to grow her social media following and “find different hobbies to do besides dance.”

“I’m like, let’s use this time to try to find some different things I can do, things that I enjoy,” she says. “I’ve always been really interested in singing and acting, and I actually might get into more of that.”
As the competition continues, Bills loves to be inspired and shocked by the celebrities’ stories and dancing abilities. Maura Higgins, who is partnered with Mark Ballas, has surprised her the most.

“I was shook when she did her foxtrot the first week. I was so pleasantly surprised,” she says of the reality star’s premiere routine that earned her the top score of the night. “And she gets so nervous and she’s so hard on herself. So the way that she was describing how it was going during rehearsals, I was like, ‘Oh, she’s going through it.’ It was insane! Mark’s such a good teacher, too, so she’s in great hands.”

Her experience on “DWTS” so far has given Bills a new perspective, she says. In the last couple of years, she’s realized that when she’s overwhelmed and consumed by her passion, she’s still grateful for the experiences she’s getting.

“Dance is a huge commitment, it takes up a lot of your life and it can be really easy to get overly consumed in it, let it go to your head and make it your whole entire life,” she says. “What’s absolutely changed the way I view dance ... is realizing that it’s, of course, very serious and I have to lock in when I need to, but at the end of the day, it’s not that serious. If I’m doing it, I want to do it because I love it and I want to have a good time.”

So while “DWTS” viewers can still catch Bills on the dance floor showcasing her skills, the pressure of competing is off. In her downtime, she’ll be relaxing at home, alone or with friends, enjoying a good meal and listening to Raye, country music or Harry Styles. She’ll also be watching “The Count of Monte Cristo” — “I’m obsessed with it,” she says – and “Sterling Point.”

“I know that me and Sarah Jane’s time was short-lived competing, but truly what a first season to have!” she says. “I’m really grateful and honored to have been partnered with Sarah Jane. I’m having the best time ever, I’m just trying to learn and keep growing — and I love the show.”

title: Dylan Sprouse Reveals ‘Lovely’ Name of 1st Child with Barbara Palvin
summary: Dylan Sprouse and Barbara Palvin have welcomed their first child!
story: Dylan Sprouse and Barbara Palvin have welcomed their first child!
The former “Suite Life of Zack and Cody” star, 33, and his model wife, 32, announced on Instagram on Sept. 28 that Palvin has given birth to a baby girl.

The diehard Los Angeles Dodgers fans shared a photo holding their baby girl dressed in a Dodgers onesie while watching the team play. Palvin is decked out in a Shohei Ohtani jersey, and Sprouse wears a Miguel Rojas jersey.
“We took Labor Day literally this year,” Palvin captioned the photo.
Palvin confirmed they welcomed a daughter by posting a photo to her Instagram story of Sprouse holding the infant close and captioning it, “Daddy’s girl already.”
Sprouse also revealed his daughter’s name on the Sept. 29 episode of his “Wildmen” podcast: Sylvie.
“She’s very lovely. Her name is Sylvie,” Sprouse said. “Sylvie Sprouse. She’s a very well behaved baby.”

The little girl will watch her first Dodgers playoff games this year when the two-time defending World Series champions play the winner of this week’s Braves-Phillies series in the National League Division Series, which begins on Oct. 3 at Dodger Stadium.

In May, Sprouse and Palvin announced on Instagram that they were expecting their first child. Their joint post featured a sonogram image of a baby’s hand making a “rock on” symbol. A second image showed Sprouse and Palvin’s hands making the same gesture.
The couple’s announcement came the same day Palvin showed off a baby bump alongside Sprouse at the Cannes Film Festival in France.
The two have been married since July 2023. They got engaged in September 2022 after five years of dating.

title: The Best Principal Ever? Mr. Belding Was the Guiding Voice on ‘Saved by the Bell’
summary: Mr. Belding, the principal on “Saved by the Bell” played by Dennis Haskins, has died. Here’s a look back on his legacy
story: If you’re in your 40s or 50s, there’s a good chance you woke up this morning to a flurry of text messages from friends sharing a link that “Saved by the Bell” star Dennis Haskins had died.

Haskins, who died at the age of 75, played Mr. Belding, the principal of fictional Bayside High School on the long-running 1990s Saturday morning franchise. He cared deeply about his students, while playing the foil to the scheming Zack Morris, played by Mark-Paul Gosselaar.

Armed with a catch phrase — “Hey, hey, hey, what is going on here?” — the perpetually cheery and often exasperated Mr. Belding was somewhat frazzled and a step behind Zack and the Bayside crew, but he always caught on and always led them on the straight and narrow. He was funny, but he was caring, the kind of adult kids enjoyed watching on Saturday mornings.

There’s a place for Mr. Belding on the Mount Rushmore of fictional principals. Haskins’ combination of comic timing, compassion and chemistry with the cast congealed to make Mr. Belding a beloved character, complete with a silly name that elicited images of a goofball that belied his intelligence.
“A cranky editor from Universal,” “Saved by the Bell” producer Peter Engel told TODAY.com in 2019 about who the inspiration for the name was.

Whether he was getting duped into improperly trimming a bonsai tree by Screech so Zack could try and win a free trip to Hawaii, freaking out when his wife went into labor after an earthquake or lending advice after Slater mourned the death of his pet chameleon, Mr. Belding was a rock, the kind of principal who may seem somewhat clueless and goofy on the surface, but underneath was a pillar of strength and wisdom for his students.

Haskins portrayed Mr. Belding in “Good Morning, Miss Bliss,” the original iteration of “Saved by the Bell,” and would go on to play him for all four years that “Saved by the Bell” aired on NBC. He also played him in the TV movies “Saved by the Bell: Hawaiian Style” and “Saved by the Bell: Wedding in Las Vegas.”

In addition, he played the character on an episode of “Saved by the Bell: The College Years,” and would portray him for another 143 episodes on “Saved by the Bell: The New Class” over the course of its entire seven-season run. It’s rare for one actor to be so associated with one character for so long.

Haskins is the second “Saved by the Bell” cast member to die, following Dustin Diamond, who died in 2021. Diamond, who played Screech, endured a complicated life after his time playing the character came to an end, but Haskins’ legacy isn’t as sad.

“Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more,” his agent, Jay Schachter, said in a statement following his death. “He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans.”
His fans also loved him. Haskins made personal appearances at everything from minor league baseball games to college campuses over the years.

If you know “Saved by the Bell,” you can conjure images of Mr. Belding going toe to toe with Zack while trying to teach him right from wrong, the threat of detention hanging overhead like the threat of a Valley prank. Zack’s capers were often thwarted by Mr. Belding, but, in the end, Zack did learn and come to appreciate his principal.

“You know, son, you’ve got something very special inside of you. I hope I’m around to see it when you let it all out,” Mr. Belding tells Zack in the graduation episode before they share a hug, representing a moment where Zack truly understands just how much Mr. Belding meant to him.
Haskins isn’t around to see the outpouring of love his fans still have for him. But, have no doubt, they do.

title: Netflix’s Hockey Romance ‘Icebreaker’ Casts its 2 Leads
summary: Netflix has announced the two leads taking center of the ice in their upcoming series “Icebreaker,” based off the bestselling novel by Hannah Grace.
story: Netflix has announced the two leads taking center of the ice in their upcoming series “Icebreaker,” based off the bestselling novel by Hannah Grace.
Daisy Jelley and Connor Simos have been announced to play the series’ leading couple, Anastasia “Stassie” Allen and Nate Hawkins, for the book’s adaptation.

Anastasia Allen is a competitive figure skater with her eyes on the Olympic prize. Nate Hawkins is the equally competitive captain of the hockey team. When the two are forced to share their campus’ single ice rink for practices, things begin to heat up as the pair are forced to work together to reach their individual goals.

Grace’s “Icebreaker” was first conceived as a viral Wattpad series before being published as a novel and spending 70 consecutive weeks on the New York Times bestseller list following its release. In June, Netflix announced that it would be bringing the book to life at the BANFF World Media Festival.
The novel was also a big hit on BookTok, TikTok’s avid reading community, where fans have posted raving book reviews and potential “fan-casts” in anticipation for the TV series.

Netflix has not yet announced the show’s official release date. But with Jelley and Simos stepping into the story’s framing roles, fans should be on the look out for future cast announcements and trailers.
Here’s a closer look at our two unlikely ice-mates.
Daisy Jelley as Anastasia

Jelley will be stepping into the role of Anastasia “Stassie” Allen, a strong-willed competitive figure skater and the novel’s female protagonist. Viewers may recognize the 26-year-old English actress from her roles in “How to Have Sex” as Gemma and “Geek Girl” as Poppy.
Connor Simos as Nate
Simos will be playing Jelley’s icy counterpart and eventual love interest Nate Hawkins, the good-natured captain of the Maple Hills hockey team.
Simos is in the upcoming Chris Hemsworth thriller “Subversion.” This is his first TV role.

title: Jasmine Guy Shuts Down Criticism of Her Appearance Amid Revival of ‘A Different World’
summary: Jasmine Guy is calling out critics who have been posting negative comments about her appearance following the release of the “A Different World” revival.
story: Jasmine Guy is calling out critics who have been posting negative comments about her appearance following the release of the “A Different World” revival.

On Sept. 24, fans of the beloved sitcom were reunited with Guy and her character Whitley when the actor reprised her role in the series’ Netflix reboot. Guy was joined by Kadeem Hardison, Darryl M. Bell and Cree Summers, who all had special guest appearances in the new show.
But while many fans were happy to see Whitley, Dwayne, Ron and Freddie together again, others began comparing Guy to the ‘80s version of herself.
She reacted to the comments in an Instagram post Sept. 27.
“The internet can be brutal to women as we grow older. It asks us to celebrate life while criticizing every sign that we’ve lived it,” she said.
Guy continued, “Growing older brings change, and I won’t pretend every change is easy. But beauty, style, and joy don’t have an expiration date.”

She encouraged followers to not spend their time judging themselves or each other and instead focus on loving one another “making memories, and living the life we’re here to live.” She also added Al Green’s “Simply Beautiful” to the post.
Celebrity friends and fans applauded her uplifting message and left supportive replies.
Tina Knowles praised Guy for being an “Accomplished , Beautiful, graceful, Lady.”
Tatyana Ali called the 64-year-old actor “gorgeous” and included multiple crowns, sparkle and a red rose emoji.
Co-star Cornell Young IV, who plays Shaquille Johnson in the revival, commented, “You are so Gorgeous! Even a more Gorgeous soul! I love you.”

One fan chimed in, “You are THEEEE JASMINE GUY. An icon, then and now. The internet can be so cruel to women for simply living long enough to age, but please know so many of us see your beauty, your talent, and the legacy you’ve built. We love you!”

Despite some negative posts, Guy has been busy celebrating the return of “A Different World” on social media, sharing praise from fans about the original and the revival on her Instagram stories. Fans have also been uploading scenes from their favorite episodes of the sitcom, which ran from 1987 to 1993 for six seasons.
Guy, Summers and Bell stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Sept. 23 to chat about the Netflix show and share some behind-the-scenes stories from their time filming the original.
Guy revealed that although Whitley and Dwayne were the couple viewers rooted for, in real life Hardison was dating Summer.
“I do really love him, but he was seeing her,” Guy said about Hardison as she pointed to Summer.
She quipped that the set was “quite incestuous.”
Guy then confirmed that she dated Dominic Hoffman, who played one of Whitley’s love interests, when the show aired.
“It sounds very ‘Brady Bunch’-y,” she joked.

title: The Best Dressed Stars of the 2026 VMAs, According to 3 Fashion Experts
summary: Who are the best dressed stars from the VMAs 2026 red carpet? We asked three fashion experts
story: If there’s one red carpet where fashion rules are meant to be broken, it’s the MTV VMAs.

This year, stars leaned all the way in, serving up sheer fabrics, lace, corsets, rhinestones, dramatic silhouettes and plenty of skin. Also at the 2026 awards ceremony, Taylor Swift arrived in a “Patient Zero”-inspired dress, Adam Lambert wore a headpiece spelling out his name, Brandon Sklenar went blond and Sombr had an unforgettable belt.
Fashion experts Maggie Gillette, a principal at The Curio, Julie DuRocher, design director at Jovani, and bridal fashion designer Hayley Paige weigh in on the night’s standout style moments.
Paris Hilton
DuRocher is loving Paris Hilton’s fresh take on red carpet glamour.

“Paris Hilton is giving us a very new-age look,” DuRocher says. “I love how polished and modern it feels while still having that signature Paris glamour. It feels fresh for her and perfectly suited to the VMAs.”
Lucky Daye
The R&B singer’s Campillo ensemble was Gillette’s standout among the men’s fashion.
“The wrap detail felt so chic and I love that they used a clasp instead of buttons as a closure,” Gillette says, particularly praising the unusual fastening.
To Gillette, the detail feels like a natural progression of another menswear trend. “It felt like the evolution to the men’s brooch trend we’ve been seeing on celebs this year.”
She also loved the fabric’s subtle sheen, noting that “that’s atypical for menswear and works so well here!”
Normani
Normani’s ensemble struck DuRocher as a cool mix of sexy, feminine and fashion forward.

“I love the combination of that jersey-like, leather-inspired look with the dramatic flower at the dropped torso and the fit-and-flare silhouette,” she says. “It feels cool and fashion-forward while still being very feminine.”
For DuRocher, the overall effect is “modern pageant glamour in the best way.”
Carter Gregory
Carter Gregory, vice president of A&R at Capitol Music Group, leaned fully into rock-and-roll glamour in archival Tom Ford.
“Carter Gregory wearing archival Tom Ford was peak rock and roll,” Gillette says. She points to the leather pants and leopard print as a particularly bold combination.
The unexpected color combination also kept the ensemble feeling contemporary. The black and brown, she says, “kept this look feeling fashion forward and modern.”
Teyana Taylor
Teyana Taylor knows how to make an entrance, and both fashion experts took notice.

Gillette called Taylor’s Zuhair Murad Couture look “gothic glam at its finest,” pointing to the crochet-inspired fabric, dramatic neckline and lush feather details. The result, she says, was “red carpet alchemy.”
DuRocher was equally enthusiastic about Taylor’s revealing gown.

“This is how you wear a revealing dress to an awards show, it’s provocative, but it still feels elegant,” she says. “I love the lace and beaded detailing and the way the look plays with coverage and skin.”
Nicky Hilton
DuRocher immediately noticed the rhinestones, sheer detailing and form-fitting silhouette.
“I especially love the detail in the back. The dress itself is a wow moment,” she says.
Lisa Rinna
Lisa Rinna brought a little ’80s glamour to the VMAs, and DuRocher was here for it.
“I love the white dress paired with her short, bleached hair, the entire look feels very ’80s in the best possible way,” she says.
It’s the cohesion of the styling that really works for her. “Everything works together, from the styling to the silhouette, and she looks completely put together,” DuRocher says.
Olandria Carthen
The “Love Island” star brought early-2000s pop-star energy to the VMAs in a lace-up MMS look.
“Olandria seemed to be channeling a pop star from the early aughts in this laced up MMS look that hit on both the textural and corseting trends we saw all over the red carpet tonight,” Gillette says.
She could even picture a certain pop icon in it: “I could absolutely see Christina Aguilera wearing something like this to the VMAs 25 years ago.”
Gillette also loved the way Carthen modernized the look with the red details and feminine bow at the hem, which played against the tougher leather.
Sienna Spiro
Sienna Spiro, who won the award for best new artist, caught DuRocher’s eye for an entirely different reason: intricate femininity.
“Sienna Spiro’s gown is so intricate and delicate,” she says. “I love the detailing throughout the dress and the way it feels incredibly feminine while still making an impact on the carpet.”
“The shape and embellishment give it a beautiful sense of glamour without feeling overdone,” DuRocher says.
Lisa
Lisa made a case for red and then doubled down with an oversized matching jacket.
“Lisa looks spectacular,” DuRocher says. “I love the red dress paired with that big, oversized red jacket, it feels bold, glamorous and incredibly current.”
She also sees the outfit as a snapshot of two major trends coming together. “Red is having such a moment right now, and so is lace, so I love seeing those trends come together here.”
Troye Sivan
Troye Sivan, the Australian singer, took a more unexpected approach in Erdem, and Gillette loved the contrast.

“The interplay between the masculine suit with the very high almost Edwardian collar against the draped silk and feathers is such a strong contrast especially since everything is in black and super crisp optic white,” she says.
Taylor Swift
“There’s something deliciously dark about this,” Paige says. “It’s almost ‘Practical Magic’ witchery, but rendered in liquid shimmer.”

The juxtaposition gives the look a sense of “sorceress” glamour, while the silver draping adds a touch of disco, she says. The asymmetry, Paige adds, keeps all that drama in Tamara Ralph’s couture collectionfeeling effortless rather than overworked.
Shaboozey

“Entirely rock star,” Paige says. “The leather three-piece could have gone costume very quickly, but the lean proportions, skinny tie, statement buckle and cropped trouser keep it feeling intentional rather than too theatrical.”

The combination gives the look an “outlaw-meets-frontman energy,” she says. The result feels polished without losing its edge, “like he might accept an award and then immediately disappear onto a tour bus.”

title: How Many VMAs Has Taylor Swift Won?
summary: How many VMAs does Taylor Swift have? She just set a record by winning 33.
story: Taylor Swift has a long history with the MTV VMAs and just broke yet another record.
Swift received her 33rd moon person at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMAs history. She was previously tied with Beyoncé with 30 awards.

Swift won three VMAs at the 2026 ceremony on Sept. 27, including the inaugural Artist Director Honors, which honors artists’ work behind the camera to make music videos. In her acceptance speech, Swift said she’s made 60 music videos and wrote and directed 18.

Swift also won the VMA for best direction for “Opalite” and the night’s marquee award, video of the year, for “The Fate of Ophelia.” Both tracks are from her 12th studio album “The Life of a Showgirl,” which was just rereleased as a special “The Encore” edition with four new tracks.
Swift became the most awarded solo artist in VMAs history after the 2024 ceremony, at which she won seven total trophies. That brought her career total to 30, tying her with Beyoncé at the time.
Beyoncé has won 26 VMAs as a solo artist, two with Destiny’s Child and two with her husband, Jay-Z, as The Carters, according to the Guinness Book of World Records.
Over the years, Swift has taken home moon people for “You Belong With Me,” “Blank Space,” “You Need to Calm Down,” “Anti-Hero” and more songs from her different eras.

title: ‘Zoolander’ Turns 25: Ben Stiller Promoted His Comedy on TODAY in 2001 After a Heavy Time for the Country
summary: In 2001, Ben Stiller spoke with TODAY about “Zoolander” coming out less than three weeks after the Sept. 11 terror attacks.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Ben Stiller, who stopped by the show on Sept. 28, 2001 to talk about his movie “Zoolander,” which came out in the wake of the Sept. 11 terror attacks.

Comedy was in an unprecedented situation of uncertainty after the events of Sept. 11. No one knew when, or if, the country would be ready to laugh again, as a reeling country continued to mourn the terror attacks. It was into this uncharted environment that Ben Stiller found himself when “Zoolander” was released in theaters on Sept. 28, 2001.

That same day, Stiller appeared on TODAY with Katie Couric, not just to talk about the film that poked fun at the modeling industry, but also the circumstances under which it would be served up to the public.
“You’re hoping to provide people with some much needed escapism,” Couric said.
“Yeah, just (a) distraction,” Stiller replied.

As it turned out, there was an appetite for comedy and Derek Zoolander’s famed “Blue Steel” gaze. The movie would open in second place, en route to a $45 million take at the domestic box office. The film eventually became a favorite in the Stiller canon and spawned a sequel in 2016.
What Did Ben Stiller Say About Releasing ‘Zoolander’ After 9/11?

“It’s a really strange time to just be talking about movies and entertainment because it just all kind of does seem frivolous,” he said. “For me, like having the movie come out now, the toughest thing about it. I thought it was a good idea to be able to have a comedy for people to go to if they wanted to, to have that option. But talking about it seems kind of not important.”
Stiller, who co-wrote, co-produced, starred in and directed “Zoolander,” called it a “really silly, ridiculous comedy” that he had seen since the attacks, but before it was officially released.

“Everything is different now,” he said. “But the great thing about seeing it, I’ve seen it with some audiences since this, and people are laughing. And it does seem to at least kind of be so silly that it kind of takes them out of stuff for awhile. But, definitely, everything’s different now.”
What Did Ben Stiller Think About Skewering the Fashion Industry?

When it came to poking fun at the fashion industry, Stiller said, “I can relate to it because we, in show business, I think sometimes take ourselves a little too seriously, get wrapped up in our own craziness.”
Adding, “In a way, it’s kind of like, working out some of those demons, not just kind of making fun of the modeling industry because that’s pretty easy.”
How Did ‘Zoolander’ Land So Many Celebrity Cameos?

“Zoolander” featured some serious star power in small roles. David Bowie, Lenny Kravitz, Winona Ryder, Gwen Stefani, Christian Slater, Donald Trump and Lance Bass are just some of the people who had cameos.
“Everybody kind of wanted to just have fun. It’s a real, like I said, it’s a silly movie, so they read the script and it just kind of felt like a fun thing to do,” Stiller said.

title: Adam Lambert Shocks Crowd With Surprise Performance During VMAs George Michael Tribute
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
story: Surprise!

The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
The homage comes a decade after the pop legend and queer icon died on Christmas Day 2016 at age 53.
Lambert, joined by several other artists including singer Meek and MNEK, belted out the 1990 hit. Several in the crowd were brought to their feet during the performance.

The tribute also featured Sombr, who performed Michael’s hit songs “Faith” and “Father Figure,” Raye, who performed “Knew You Were Waiting,” and Teddy Swims who sang a rendition of “Careless Whisper.”
During his portion, Sombr also wore a black Harley-Davidson jacket that originally worn by Michael during his 1988 Faith Tour, according to Vogue.
“To wear a jacket that has become so synonymous with that era was pretty surreal, and an honor,” Sombr told the magazine.

Michael, who won a host of VMAs, including the Video Vanguard lifetime achievement award in 1989, was highly regarded as a pioneering artist in the pop music scene, making a significant impact both as one-half of the duo Wham! and also as a solo artist.
While the icon was known for his many musical hits, he is also remembered as a champion of the LGBTQ+ community and philanthropist, who used his platform to help find a cure for HIV and AIDS.

Michael was outed as gay in 1998 following an incident in Beverly Hills during which he was arrested for engaging in a lewd act at a public toilet. Michael later roasted the ordeal in his music video for “Outside,” in which he mocked the Los Angeles police officers who caught him by featuring two uniformed officers kissing.

“I’m a very proud man. I want people to know that I have not been exposed as a gay man,” Michael told CNN in a now-famous 1998 interview. “I don’t feel any shame whatsoever, and neither do I think I should.”
With his unapologetic embrace of his sexuality, the musician is credited with opening the door and empowering many other queer entertainers in the music industry.

Given his rich legacy, many fans initially called out the VMAs for its choice in tribute performers — none of whom had publicly identified as a member of the LGBTQ+ community. MTV had announced exclusively in Rolling Stone Sept. 22 that acts Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims would be performing. Many felt that without performers who reflected Michael’s activism and identity, the LGBTQ community was being snubbed.

“You’d think with George being an icon for the LGBT community, they’d get someone like Sam Smith or Troye Sivan involved,” one user wrote on social media platform Reddit, referencing other openly gay pop icons.
While no other artists were announced ahead of the awards, singer Adam Lambert posted a cryptic Instagram story which featured Michael’s song “Freedom ‘90.”

title: Britain believes Iran was involved in incident near air base used by U.S., prime minister says
summary: Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorist offenses in the incident outside RAF Fairford. Iran had denied any involvement.
story: LONDON — There are strong indications Tehran played a part in a security incident outside a British air base that U.S. forces use to facilitate strikes on Iran, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday.

Burnham said he had chaired an emergency security meeting this week after the incident, which happened early Sunday. Five men, all British nationals, were arrested on suspicion of terrorist and explosives offenses and were released on bail this week.
“We have been waiting to confirm what we could say, but we can now confirm our belief that Iran played a part,” he said in an interview with Sky News.
“This remains, though, a complex and very serious police investigation, so I can’t say any more at this stage,” he added.
The British Parliament is in recess, but Burnham said he “wouldn’t hesitate” to recall lawmakers “should that be necessary.”
Iran has denied any involvement in the incident.

“The embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in London categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran to arrest of five suspects in the vicinity of RAF Fairford base,” the Iranian Embassy in Britain said in a statement Monday on X.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday on X that Burnham was wrongly accusing Iran of having played a role in the incident.

“PM Burnham says the UK Government ‘can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part’ in the RAF Fairford incident,” Araghchi wrote. “I can confirm Iran’s belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all. You’re barking up the wrong tree.”
President Donald Trump told reporters Wednesday that the U.S. is closely examining the incident.
Asked whether he was planning any response to Iran, Trump replied: “Well, we are. Look, we are studying it right now. We’re studying it. We’re studying it very hard.”
Add to Google
Add to Google

“U.K. did release a number of people that we caught wanting to blow up a base,” Trump added. “We caught them early, and I’m trying to figure out if that’s for real — that they actually did it. Maybe they did it for a reason, but we’re going to know about that this afternoon, so we’ll report on that.”
In an interview with Fox News on Wednesday night, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel had provided intelligence to the U.K. about an attack.
“We gave the Brits the intel that there was going to be an attack, and it’s an Iranian-sponsored attack,” Netanyahu said, without providing additional details.
Burnham’s statements were based on intelligence that has been gathered as a result of the investigation, two senior U.S intelligence officials briefed on the matter told NBC News.
Two calls early Sunday U.K. time alerted authorities that the five people could have been up to something inappropriate, according to one official.
One call to police came from one of the five men in the group at about 12:45 a.m., the official said.
British media previously reported that call.
A local farmer called police around 1:30 a.m. local time — a call that police initially cited as the reason for the tip on the group’s activities, the official said.

No charges have been filed against the men, all in their 20s and from London, who were arrested after three vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a British air force station about 90 minutes west of London.
Counterterrorism police later took over the case after a major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated, disrupting life in the normally quiet, rural community of the Cotswolds.

title: U.S. pressures European allies to release diesel reserves as Trump considers export ban
summary: The Trump administration asked European allies to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
story: The Trump administration has asked several European allies to release diesel fuel from their national emergency stockpiles in an effort to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
The average U.S. price of diesel has soared by 70% since the war with Iran began, hitting $6.38 per gallon Thursday, according to AAA.
Less than five weeks before the U.S. midterm elections, Republicans are eager for any way to lower domestic fuel prices.
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright appeared confident this week that Europe would agree to tap its diesel reserves.

“You will hear announcements from our friends in Europe about new diesel supplies that’ll come to the market that’ll meaningfully push diesel prices down,” he told reporters Wednesday at an event with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office.
But U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stopped well short of suggesting the European release was a done deal.
“I spoke with my French counterpart” about a diesel release, he said Thursday, calling it a “very good conversation.”
“I let him know that this is an idea that we’ve had in the U.S.,” he told Bloomberg Television. “We’d love to have a collaborative response to this.”

The United States is hosting G20 trade ministers in Milwaukee this week, where Greer said he planned to meet his European Union counterpart. Also in Milwaukee are trade ministers from China, India, the United Kingdom and other countries affected by tight global diesel supplies.
The message coming from Europe on Thursday was also a cautious one.
The E.U. is “in very close contact with our member states on this ongoing issue,” European Commission energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen told reporters at a media briefing in Brussels.
“We are also having high-level contacts ongoing with the U.S. administration,” she said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The majority of Europe’s emergency diesel reserves are stored in Germany and France. Both American and European oil refineries have been running at near full capacity for months, churning out as much diesel fuel as possible.

While the Iran war is responsible for the lion’s share of price increases in crude oil and unleaded gasoline around the world, the price of diesel has been outpacing both of them since July, albeit for a different reason.
Russia has traditionally been a major exporter of diesel, but that stopped this summer after Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed Russian refineries.
On July 8, Russia banned the export of diesel in order to preserve its domestic supply. On Wednesday, the Kremlin extended that ban until the end of October.

“We’re tight on diesel because we’ve lost diesel exports from Russia,” Wright said at the White House. “We’ve lost diesel, some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we’re restoring those. And we’ve lost diesel exports from China.”
“That’s a lot of interruptions,” he said.

But whether Europe will tap its emergency reserves of diesel to increase global supply is complicated by the fact that the Trump administration is actively considering a move that is effectively the opposite of what it is asking Europe to do.
On Wednesday, the president mused about imposing a ban on exports of U.S. diesel.
“I’m thinking about it,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “I speak to Chris and Doug about it a lot,” he said, referring to Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
“They sort of think ... it’ll help diesel, but it might raise the price of other things,” he said.
An export ban on U.S. diesel would hit European countries particularly hard.
It would also land at a moment when average U.S. prices for unleaded gas remain almost 50% higher than they were on Feb. 28, the day the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: U.S. ends ISIS-fighting mission in Iraq as regional security fears mount
summary: Kurdish officials are worried the Biden-era decision was being carried out after Iranian missiles pummeled them this year.
story: The last American troops assigned to fight ISIS in Iraq pulled out of the country Wednesday, ending the mission that dismantled the extremists’ self-declared caliphate but raising fears about what might fill the vacuum as the Iran war grinds on.

Though the Iraqi government welcomed the end of Operation Inherent Resolve, Kurdish officials in the north of the country said they were concerned the Biden-era decision was being carried out even after Iranian missiles pummeled them following the war launched by the United States and Israel earlier this year.

Iran-backed militias in Iraq have attacked U.S. personnel and diplomats, as well as regional allies such as Saudi Arabia. And there are fears Tehran could seek to capitalize on the U.S. withdrawal, with its proxies already celebrating the move, coupled with concerns about a potential resurgence in attacks by the remnants of the Islamic State terrorist group itself.

“We came to fight a caliphate, and there is no longer a caliphate, so we are going home,” President Donald Trump said at the White House on Wednesday, adding that the moment was a “victory for the United States,” as well as a “decisive victory over ISIS, which has been completely decimated, which is the reason we went in there in the first place.”

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the “orderly departure” marked “the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated ISIS in Iraq,” in a statement Wednesday. “This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organized military threat in Iraq and across the region.”

The 2014 U.S.-led mission was successful in dismantling the “caliphate” ISIS governed across around 40% of Iraq and one-third of Syria, sweeping through that territory amid instability that followed the U.S. invasion and subsequent withdrawal.
But ISIS has not been defeated entirely in Iraq.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The group comprises “hundreds of fighters” across seven provincial units, according to a United Nations monitoring report in August. This “limited presence” in desert areas generates $500,000 annually through extortion of farmers and shepherds, the report said. But it is “unable to conduct significant attacks” and is only capable of “unsophisticated operations” following the killing and arrest of leaders, it said.

The U.S. expects Iraqi and Kurdish forces to now “lead the continuing effort to secure Iraq and keep ISIS remnants suppressed,” Parnell’s statement said. The Pentagon will “continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners.”
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who has been lavished with praise by Trump since entering office in July, described the withdrawal as the beginning of “a new phase.”

At a handover ceremony in Baghdad, he said this would be “defined by Iraq’s sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, the unity of its decision-making and balanced partnerships with its friends.”

However, Kurdish officials, who govern the north of Iraq, expressed alarm at the move. The Kurdish Peshmerga Affairs Ministry, which oversees defense, said Monday that the U.S. leaving without establishing any other air defense was “deeply concerning.”
The withdrawal was agreed to under President Joe Biden’s administration in 2024, long before the Iran war drastically changed the region’s security landscape.

The Peshmerga Ministry said Monday that 1,000 ballistic missiles have been fired at its territory by Iran since late February. “Some have hit civilian areas, inflicting injuries, material damage and deaths,” it said, nevertheless expressing “sincere gratitude” to the U.S. and its partners “for their cooperation and support.”

The 2003 U.S.-led invasion saw around 150,000 American troops enter the country, toppling leader Saddam Hussein but also triggering a disastrous sectarian war. That combat operation came to an end in 2011, with almost all of the American personnel withdrawn.

The U.S. returned to fight ISIS in 2014, with personnel numbers peaking at almost 9,000 as of 2017. That operation wound down in 2024, and until this week only a small contingent of around 1,500 remained in the Kurdish-governed north.
After this week, a smaller contingent of U.S. forces will stay in Iraq to protect American diplomats.

Iran-backed militant groups have already celebrated the milestone as “a ​historic victory,” as put by Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in the powerful umbrella group the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, who described it as “a crushing defeat for the American project.”

And though depleted, ISIS itself “is seeking to send a message that the group is still powerful and capable of launching bloody attacks,” according to Col. Khalid al-Bayati, a senior security official in the strategic oil town of Kirkuk.

title: Iran ‘fully prepared’ for war to resume but diplomacy not over yet, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says
summary: Despite Trump’s comments rejecting a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said Iran hadn’t yet officially responded to the proposal.
story: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said his country is prepared to resume fighting with the United States but has not yet abandoned diplomacy after President Donald Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

“We are fully prepared for the time for the war to be resumed, and I repeat, we stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war,” Araghchi told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday, when asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Trump could seek to resume bombing after the U.S. midterm elections. “At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”

Iran had offered a deal last week to reopen the strait and resume normal maritime passage through the critical global oil chokepoint within seven days, as part of a plan conveyed to the U.S. through mediator Qatar on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Trump said Saturday that he had turned down that proposal, telling reporters: “I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly.”
Araghchi told moderator Kristen Welker on Sunday that despite Trump’s public comments, the rejection had still not been officially communicated to Iran via mediators.

He reaffirmed that Iran was ready to reopen the strait as part of an agreement to end the conflict, adding that in return, “we want our monies, our assets, which are illegally frozen, to be released. We want to be able to sell our oil.”

Araghchi said the conditions were “not new” and were things the U.S. has already committed itself to previously, referring to the memorandum of understanding that the two countries signed in June that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. That agreement collapsed within days after fresh strikes were exchanged.
“If you ask us, there is no reason why we should go back to diplomacy,” Araghchi said. “But I am still trying diplomacy because I think we shouldn’t miss any chance for peace.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“We don’t care about U.S. midterm elections,” the Iranian official added. “We care about our national interests.”

Prior to Araghchi’s interview, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told “Meet the Press” that the deal was rejected for “a number of reasons,” suggesting the U.S. could not permit Iran “to have access to billions in frozen funds.”

Waltz said: “I think this was a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable, to ask for the release of the blockade, the sanctions, international sanctions and access to billions in assets.”
He also questioned “who’s calling the shots in Iran right now,” adding that the country had violated the past memorandum of understanding by attacking international shipping.

“I think it’s kind of common sense that the president doesn’t have a lot of confidence this time after we just tried a few months ago,” Waltz added. “What I can tell you is the president will leave all options on the table to ensure the world is safe from Iran holding the world hostage with a nuclear weapon.”
Asked what deal Trump would accept, Waltz said: “I’m not going to negotiate for the president.”
“This is about keeping the next generation safe from Iran threatening the world with a nuclear weapon,” he added.
Trump said last week he was still considering whether to “annihilate” Iran or make a deal.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November midterms. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.

title: How an American teacher’s $5,000 donation helped turn a Chinese desert into a lush forest
summary: Ronald Sakolsky couldn’t believe his eyes when he visited China’s Mu Us Desert for the first time in 26 years. “Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he said.
story: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.

What was once a vast, dry desert in northern China has transformed into a lush, green forest of 50,000 full-grown trees, thanks in part to a $5,000 donation he made more than a quarter-century ago to a local farmer and “sand-control worker” named Yin Yuzhen.
Sakolsky, 69, a retired teacher from Pennsylvania, was amazed to see the transformation in China’s Inner Mongolia region last month when he visited for the first time in 26 years.
“Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he told Chinese state media. “I saw pictures, I was told all about it, but until you see it is when you realize that it’s real.”

Sakolsky and Yin’s reunion last month has been held up by Chinese authorities as an example of how China and the United States, the world’s two biggest greenhouse gas emitters, can work together on global issues such as climate change.

title: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman is evicted from her home of 70 years
summary: An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
story: An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who is a wheelchair user, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.

Supporters had gathered outside her building overnight on Friday, with dozens of police officers holding them back as some tried to stop the eviction from going ahead. In a social media video posted Friday by the Madrid tenants union, Abascal gave thanks for the support she had received.
Abascal’s lawyer, Beatriz Duro, described the force used in the eviction as “completely disproportionate and unnecessary” and decried the intransigence of the building’s owners.

The case has brought new attention to an ongoing housing crisis in major cities across Spain, as gentrification has caused rents to skyrocket and the stock of affordable housing to shrink, leading to fierce public anger.

On Saturday, tens of thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction, some setting off flares. They carried placards reading “Not one more eviction, not one less neighbor, we are all Maricarmen” and “right to housing at a fair price.”

At the end of the march, protesters sat down in the Puerta del Sol plaza, some pitching tents. They remained in place early Sunday as dozens of activists staged a sit-in. A model of a vulture, decrying so-called vulture funds, hung above the camp.
Earlier in the week, tenants unions and other housing groups held protests and rallies in 16 cities, including Granada, Logroño and Zaragoza.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
An investment fund acquired Abascal’s building in 2018 and sought a steep increase in her rent, and she had been fighting eviction for more than five years, according to the Madrid tenants union.

Duro said court officials and representatives of the fund, Urbagestión, had refused to suspend the eviction despite a pending court filing, humanitarian appeals and evidence that public authorities were working to secure alternative accommodation.

“They’re all inhumane,” Abascal said in a Spanish television interview the day before her eviction. “It’s as if I’m living with a machete at the back of my neck, ready to be chopped off at any moment.”
Duro also said an anonymous individual had offered to cover the rent payments, but the landlord declined to sign a new lease.

“We’ve been trying to negotiate with the landlords right up until the last moment, and they’ve flatly refused everything,” she said, decrying “a lack of humanity” in her treatment and “all these public resources” channeled into enabling the eviction.
Urbagestión did not respond to a request for comment.

The fresh wave of anger comes after protests in recent years against overtourism in Barcelona, where activists say a surge in apartments being used for short-term vacation rentals has contributed to a shortage of affordable housing.
The European Union announced new rules earlier this month aimed at tackling the housing crunch caused by short-term rentals in tourism hot spots.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the eviction as “a social tragedy that we cannot accept either as a country or, of course, from the perspective of public institutions.”

Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Sánchez accused Madrid’s conservative regional government of pursuing luxury penthouses while ignoring demand for social housing.

Irene Hernández López, a 31-year-old test engineer living and renting in Chamberí, about 2 miles from Retiro, said what had happened to Abascal was “outrageous,” and she was worried similar evictions were already happening to other tenants around the city.
“Housing has become a product that people do business with,” she told NBC News. “It no longer matters that it’s your personal world, where you live and where you do your life.”

Hernández López, who pays 500 euros ($570) for a room in an apartment she shares with two others, said that she was looking to move because the property was old and needs repairs but that the rental market in Madrid was “terrible,” with prices “rising extremely quickly” and very little available.

“Some rooms are 500 euros or 600 euros and you think, ‘How am I supposed to live here? How can I pay 500 euros for this?’” she said. “I do think prices should be regulated, because wages aren’t going up while housing prices keep increasing. I don’t know how we’re supposed to keep going.”
Dan Nicander, secretary-general for the International Union of Tenants, said the situation in Spain was something his organization had seen in many countries in Europe.
“It’s a part of the financialization problem, seeing housing as an asset more than a home to people,” he told NBC News.

It’s “really tough” for the people living in the houses to do anything about it, he added, saying the responsibility lay with politicians “to regulate the market in a way that it shouldn’t be that easy to buy and invest and then not [be] using the houses as homes.”
“Housing is a right,” he said. “It’s a fundamental right, first and foremost. It shouldn’t be a commodity.”

title: Europe frets as the Kremlin pushes the limits of its hybrid warfare
summary: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
story: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
After months of covert attacks and sabotage across the continent, leaders are warning that Moscow may be about to grow bolder as it seeks to sow chaos and intimidate allies of Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO’s resolve to defend members on its eastern flank or respond to attacks that fall short of all-out war, these officials say, at a time when the U.S. is distracted by other conflicts and weighing reducing its military presence in Europe.

An assessment by the Danish Defence Intelligence Service released Thursday warned that in the coming months Moscow will further intensify its campaign of so-called hybrid warfare, “with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past.” It also assessed “a low but growing risk that Russia will launch a limited military attack against one or several NATO countries bordering Russia.”
While Moscow has for years embraced tactics that straddle the threshold of war, a string of increasingly brazen incidents in recent months has alarmed U.S. allies.
‘A bit freaked out’

A key moment was the discovery of a Russian drone carrying explosives at an airport in eastern Germany near a Ukrainian aircraft last month. Berlin formally blamed Russia for what it said was a thwarted attack and imposed a diplomatic freeze, though Moscow denied involvement.

That incident appears to have changed the mindset about Russia’s growing threat in Europe, said Ed Arnold, a senior associate fellow in international security at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It just showed that Putin’s risk calculations are getting more liberal,” Arnold said. “Everyone just got a bit freaked out by that, quite frankly.”
It was followed by the unexpected visit of CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow, during which NATO was discussed.

Incidents have continued to pile up — at defense facilities in Estonia, rail networks in Poland and the power grid in Germany. Many have passed without clear attribution, only intensifying speculation.
All this against the backdrop of near-daily drone incursions into European airspace, fueling anxiety in eastern border towns.

title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.
story: Questions remain about how a pilot managed to sneak a weapon aboard a plane and stab his fellow pilot before it plunged thousands of feet in mere seconds. The attacker was thwarted, passengers said, and the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
“We were so scared. We didn’t know what was going to happen,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News on Wednesday after he and the rest of the passengers were flown to Tel Aviv.
Here is what we know about the incident and how close it came to resulting in tragedy.
What did passengers see?
Alevi described a harrowing scene aboard the flight, with people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.”
“At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” he said.
“We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.”
Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, said that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.”
Yaniv Hayun was pictured in a bloody T-shirt telling cameras he had been among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot.
At Ben Gurion Airport, after the passengers had returned to Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked Hayun, whom he later identified as a plumber.

Three others helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters. The group struggled to open the cockpit door. “I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” he said. “I started pulling the controls.”
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” he said. “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.”
“We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Who is the hero pilot?
Hailed as a hero, Indian pilot Smit ​Machchhar was credited by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on X for saving “the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.”

Even though he was bleeding heavily, Machchhar managed to unlock the door to the cockpit, Netanyahu told Fox News, allowing crew members and passengers to subdue his colleague and regain control of the plane.
The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said in a post on X that he was admitted to hospital in Tabuk, where the plane landed, and was “reported to be in stable condition.”

According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar, who was also praised on social media by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, worked with India’s SpiceJet ‌airline for more than 11 years before joining Flydubai. He has logged more than 9,750 flying hours, the profile says.

Machchhar trained as a pilot at Mainland Air in the New Zealand city of Dunedin for 18 months, beginning in 2008, the school’s CEO, Philip Kean, told the country’s 1News outlet. Machchhar “did very well” as a student and later returned to India where he worked as a recruiter for the school, Kean said.
What about the alleged attacker?
Few details have been released about the alleged attacker, including his name and his condition.
Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the incident told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the other pilot is from Oman.
Omani authorities have not commented and the Omani Foreign Ministry and the embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment from NBC News.
Netanyahu said the pilot was being investigated in Saudi Arabia, where he was detained after the flight landed.

Both Machchhar and the pilot who initiated the attack were transferred to Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Thursday, according to a statement from the Saudi Arabian Ministry of Interior, citing an unnamed “official source” at the ministry.

“The source confirmed that the pilot and his co-pilot, after their health improved and the medical team cleared them, departed the Kingdom for Abu Dhabi this morning,” the ministry said in the statement.
Was this an attack?

Based on the early results of the investigation, it increasingly looks like this was an act of terrorism, a senior American official and a Saudi Arabian official briefed on the investigation told NBC News.
Saudi Arabia confirmed an altercation between Machchhar and the co-pilot in the Ministry of Interior statement posted on Thursday.

“The source indicated that initial investigations conducted by the competent authorities in the Kingdom, with the participation of a security team from the sisterly United Arab Emirates, revealed an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries,” the ministry said in the statement.

The United Arab Emirates, which owns Flydubai, is also trying to determine “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or ‌purpose, or involved prior planning or direction,” the country’s state news agency reported Thursday.
Without providing any evidence, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Wednesday ⁠that preliminary information indicated that the pilot whom he described as a terrorist aimed to crash the plane.
Netanyahu described it as “a serious security incident.”
Speaking in the Oval Office on Wednesday, President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu “at length about this event.”
“It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” he said.
Was Iran involved?
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.

And there have been no official suggestions from Israel that the Islamic Republic was behind the attack. Two Israeli security officials told The Associated Press that Israel had not identified any Iranian involvement so far.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters at the White House that the pilot who initiated the attack could be linked to Iran.
“I would say the answer, based on what I’m hearing, is yes. But we’re working on it right now,” he said.
Asked if the pilot could have been radicalized or working with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, Trump replied, “Could have been, yeah.”
Does this alter anything for American flights?
There are “no credible threats” to U.S. airlines, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a news conference Wednesday.
But he said the U.S. took every incident like this very seriously “and we continue to look at the procedures that we have in place, and continue to make sure the American people are safe.”
What questions remain?
Aside from his nationality, little is known about the pilot who carried out the attack or his motives for doing so.
Pilots undergo rigorous screening and it is standard for airlines to vet their backgrounds and check their criminal and employment history.

They also pass through metal detectors and checkpoints at airports, so it is unclear how he snuck a weapon aboard the plane. Netanyahu said in his interview with Fox News that Machchhar had apparently been stabbed or hit with ⁠an axe.
It also remains unclear whether air marshals were on board the flight at the time of the incident.

Saudi Arabia has warned that it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about who was responsible for the incident, and Israel and the UAE have announced investigations into what exactly happened on Flydubai Flight 1073.

title: Pilot stabbed his co-pilot in apparent attempt to crash Israel-bound plane, Netanyahu says
summary: On-duty crewmembers were able to divert and land the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport, the airline said.
story: TEL AVIV — A pilot stabbed his co-pilot aboard a plane headed to Israel on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the aircraft with 174 people on board, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

“I don’t think it was a hijacking. It looks like a suicide attempt, simply because of what this hero, Yaniv, has described,” Netanyahu said on “CBS Evening News,” referring to Yaniv Hayun, a passenger who said he entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.
The pilot who initiated the attack is an Omani citizen and is being interrogated in Saudi Arabia, Netanyahu said on the CBS program on Wednesday night.
Netanyahu said a motive was being determined, including whether it was an attempt to commit an act of terrorism. He said he expected the suspect pilot would be moved to Dubai soon.
“He’ll be investigated, interrogated and we’ll join the interrogation, and find out what happened there exactly,” Netanyahu said.
President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that the attack was “an incredible story.”
“I did speak to Bibi Netanyahu at length about this event, and it seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” Trump said.
Passengers lived through scenes of terror as the Flydubai flight approaching Tel Aviv shook violently and abruptly plummeted. The flight had originated in Dubai.

“I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News. “Then I understood the weight of the actual situation.”
Alevi said he thought he was going to die as he felt the plane rapidly descend, with “screaming, people running, panicking, blood.”
Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, told NBC News that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.”
Flight data indicates the Boeing 737, flight number FZ 1073, plunged by 14,125 feet in just 29 seconds, according to Flightradar24.

All Flydubai flights to and from Israel have been temporarily suspended as authorities continue their investigation into what occurred on Flight FZ 1073, a spokesperson for the airline said in a statement.
“This temporary suspension will allow the relevant authorities to continue their work and establish all the facts surrounding the incident,” the spokesperson said in the statement.

The midair incident led to a diversion and an emergency landing at Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport, known as Tabuk Airport. A rescue flight later brought passengers to Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport.

At Ben Gurion, Netanyahu personally thanked a passenger still wearing a bloodied T-shirt, who told cameras he was among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot. Netanyahu’s office named the man as Hayun. Netanyahu later said that Hayun is a plumber in an interview on Fox News.
Hayun told Netanyahu that, as he made his way to the cockpit, the plane took a steep nose dive which knocked him sideways, according to the Israeli government press office.
Three other passengers helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters at Ben Gurion.
The group struggled to open the cockpit door.
“We managed to get it open, but what made it difficult for us was the pilot himself — he had been stabbed and was on the other side of the door,” he said.
Netanyahu said on the CBS program that when Hayun went in the cockpit he saw the pilot who had initiated the attack trying to crash the plane.
“He wasn’t sitting in the pilot seat, trying to stabilize the plane, he was trying to jam the equipment,” Netanyahu said.
Hayun told Netanyahu that he confronted the pilot who had initiated the attack, according to the Israeli government press office.
“I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” Hayun said. “I started pulling the controls.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Hayun told Netanyahu that he took actions based on what he had seen on a TV show and helped stabilize the plane, according to the Israeli government press office.
“Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” Hayun said.
“It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation,” Hayun added. “We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top.”

Israeli officials also praised the stabbed pilot, identified as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, for his actions in opening the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to rush in, secure the cockpit and prevent the plane from crashing.
“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals,” Netanyahu said on X. “I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery. He is a true hero.”
In the interview on Fox News, Netanyahu said that there were 30 children on the plane.
Video from on board appeared to show two people lying on the floor, visibly bloodied as others crowd around them.
Machchhar is in stable condition in a hospital in Saudi Arabia, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.
Four U.S. citizens, who are dual nationals, were on the flight, per two U.S. officials.
Prime minister’s spokesperson Doron Spielman said that “there is a strong opinion” that the incident was a terror attack, “but we can’t be sure until we debrief everybody.”
No country or terror organization has claimed the incident.
Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the investigation also told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the co-pilot is from Oman.
The officials did not name that pilot.
The Omani Embassy in the U.S. did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
An investigation by Saudi authorities is ongoing, David Mencer, a spokesperson for the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, said.

The stabbing increasingly looks like an act of terrorism based on the early results from the investigation, according to a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation and a Saudi official briefed on the investigation.

The spokesperson for the Saudi Embassy in the U.S., Hessa Alyahya, said authorities were waiting to determine whether the attack was a dispute between the pilots or whether it was an act sponsored by Iran or the Houthis. She said it was expected that more would be known within 24 hours.

Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, deputy prime minister and foreign affairs minister of the United Arab Emirates, and Israel’s foreign affairs minister, Gideon Saar, spoke on the phone Wednesday afternoon.

According to the UAE Foreign Affairs Ministry, Al Nahyan asked about the safety of passengers on the Flydubai flight, which had “experienced a security incident that was successfully brought under control” and wished “good health and well-being” for the passengers.
There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in today’s attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.
The preliminary Israeli investigation strongly suggests that the incident was an attempted terrorist attack by the Omani pilot who stabbed his co-pilot, the official said.
Netanyahu said on CBS that it was too early to tell if there was any Iranian involvement.

“We’ve had signs that Iran, in particular through its proxies, was intending to heighten terrorist attacks against Israel and Israeli nationals abroad,” Netanyahu said. “But I think it’s too early to say whether there was Iranian collusion here. I think we’ll find out. It won’t take a long time.”
The aircraft was “successfully secured” and landed by on-duty crew traveling on board, Flydubai said.

“At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation,” the airline said, adding: “We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts.”
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz meanwhile told Israeli media the incident “was a jihadist terrorist attack attempt,” without saying how he reached that conclusion.

After hours on the ground in Saudi Arabia, the diverted passengers were brought back to Ben Gurion Airport, where they were greeted by well-wishers waving Israeli flags and reunited with family members.
Some of those returning waved to the cameras and discussed their experiences, while exhausted parents carried their young children through the terminal.
Peleg Itali, 17, said there was a family with small children near him on the flight.
“The mother doesn’t even know what to tell them,” he said. “No one knows everything, because no one knew what was going on.”

At least one person, a passenger in his 50s, was taken to a hospital with a “chest injury,” said Aryeh Myers, a paramedic with Magen David Adom, Israel’s national emergency agency. Myers described the person’s health condition as “mild.”
Earlier, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee expressed relief on X that the incident didn’t turn out to be “more serious.”
